title: Press a contact plate flat on a surface for 10 s
instruction: Take a surface sample inside the marked circle with the contact plate, then put the plate back in its lid on the tray and let go.
context: Why: USP <797> requires every sterile-compounding pharmacy to sample its work surfaces, with contact plates or swabs, at least monthly, and drug and food plants do it every shift; in 2012 contaminated compounded injections caused a fungal meningitis outbreak with 750 cases and 64 deaths (CDC). A robot that samples surfaces to the maker's method frees technicians and makes the press repeatable. The method: the plate's agar, standing 1.5 mm proud of its rim, is pressed onto the surface and incubated. The plate maker's instructions (after NF EN ISO 18593): open the plate, apply the agar directly to the surface and keep a uniform pressure, for example 500 g for 10 s, then close the plate. A tap, a rocked or dragged press, or a push until the rim comes down gives an incomplete or smeared imprint, and agar touched to anything else is a contaminated sample. Done by: environmental-monitoring technicians and QC microbiologists in pharmaceutical, hospital-pharmacy and food plants.
setup: On the table, 200 mm in front of the robot and 190 mm right of the centre line: a 120 x 120 x 3 mm PP sample tray. On it a 65 mm agar contact plate (Biokar/Solabia pre-poured contact plate, polystyrene plastic, about 1 USD) stored the usual way, agar down: its lid (70 mm OD x 9 mm, 10 g) lies open side up on the tray and the base (65 mm OD x 16 mm, 25 g with its agar) rests on the lid's inner ledge 5 mm up, so the agar, which stands 1.5 mm proud of the base's rim as a 57 mm convex disc, hangs 2.5 mm off the lid floor. Centred 260 mm in front of the robot and 20 mm left of the centre line: a 200 x 200 x 2 mm stainless steel sampling plate on a 3 kg x 0.1 g bench scale (200 x 200 x 30 mm), its top 32 mm above the table, tared, with an 85 mm circle of yellow tape on it (the sampling site), dusted with fluorescent tracer powder inside the circle for the real trial. Two parallel-gripper arms, three cameras.
scoring: Tools: the bench scale (grams; 100 g = 0.98 N) with its display in the side camera's view, the video's timer, the tracer imprint on the agar under a UV torch, and a ruler. Read on the imprint: a flat still press leaves one full 57 mm disc; a tilt over 3 deg leaves part of the disc blank (a crescent); a slide leaves a streak, its length measured with the ruler. A touch is the agar on the surface with at least 0.5 N. A press counts while the scale reads 300-700 g (3-7 N), the plate's centre is within 10 mm of the circle's centre and the plate is within 3 deg of flat. 0: anything else, including the untouched start, or a latched 0. 0.25: the agar pressed on the surface at 3 N or more with the plate's centre within 10 mm of the circle's centre. 0.5: one continuous press held for at least 9 s (the maker's 10 s, less 1 s of tolerance for the video timer). 0.75: also only one touch, the plate never slid more than 2 mm during it, never pressed over 7 N (the rim never came down), and the base seated back in its lid (centred within 3 mm, rim on the ledge), agar down. 1.0: all of 0.75, plus the closed plate on the tray, both grippers at least 30 mm from the plate, and nothing moving more than 2 mm for 1 s. Latched 0: the agar touches anything other than the sampling plate (lid floor, tray, table or a gripper), or the plate falls off the table or tips over.
reset_notes: Use a fresh plate each trial, stored agar down on its lid on the tray; wipe the sampling plate with 70% ethanol, re-dust the tracer in the circle and tare the scale.
fidelity: Full-size plate, lid, tray and sampling plate built from boxes; the round walls are rings of flat plates. The agar is a disc on a slider in the base: a 5 N/mm spring over its 1.5 mm, after which the rim meets the surface (real agar is stiffer). The press force is that spring's force; flatness and slide read the base's pose; agar touching anything else is read from its compression off the sampling plate. No microbes or tracer are simulated.
